subject: Problems due to linear seperation in rxLogit

messages.author: 5f6c0a60f6f91053
messages.subject: Problems due to linear seperation in rxLogit
parts:
Hello,

 

I am currently evaluating Revolution R as a data analytics platform for our company. One oft he problems I ran into during the evaluation concerns the rxLogit function. I hope you can help solve this problem.

 

I have a dataset with which I want to perform a logistic regression. I think, there are several variables with linear seperation, since I get the following error message, when performing rxLogit in the local compute context:

 

Warning: One or more fitted probabilities were numerically 0 or 1 during estimation

 

However, I still get a result. When I perform the same rxLogit computation in Teradata (not local), the computation aborts with the following error message and returns no result:

 

in UDF/XSP/UDM revoAnalytics_Zqht2.revoAnalyticsTblOp: SQLSTATE U0005: R Error on Node: 40 AMP: 55

Error in rxCall("RxLogit", params) :

Error:  Error in rxCall("RxLogit", params) :

 

Error in rxuHandleClusterJobTryFailure(retObject, hpcServerJob, autoCleanup,  :

 Error completing job on cluster:

Error in rxCall("RxLogit", params) :  

 

Why does the rxLogit function behave differently in the different computation contexts? Is there a way to perform the computation in the Database (e.g. ignoring linear seperation)?

 

Thank you and best regards

GN

messages.author: 88275a537c4bd7d2
messages.subject: Re: Problems due to linear seperation in rxLogit
parts:
Hi Guenther,

rxLogit is part of Revolution R Enterprise, but it's not included in Revolution R Open (which this group discusses). Your best bet is to contact Revolution Analytics support who will be happy to help you.

Revolution Analytics technical supprt is at: https://revolutionanalytics.zendesk.com/home 

Cheers,
# David Smith
